also: am I keeping you from something?

terms.grammar: num expects the answer no; dētineō, keep back, detain
terms.comment: Dētinēre is classical in this sense (dētinēre aliquem et dēmorārī, Lentulus in Cic. Fam. 12.15, Lewis & Short s.v. dēmoror); the question itself is Traupman’s. “I won’t keep you”: nē diūtius vōs dēmorer (Cic. de Or. 2.235, Lewis & Short).

sources: Lewis & Short: detineo · Lewis & Short: demoror
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 101, checked against the searchable text and the page image (12 November 2026).
